title: L-valine and mitochondrial flux in WOREE
summary: A conditional preclinical comparator for substrate supply and oxidative recovery.

graph.hypothesis: Valine flux can favor supply or overflow.

evidence: With valine restriction, brain valine fell about 42% in WT and 1% in primary ECHS1-deficient mice. The mutant intervention did not measurably improve the provoked seizure outcomes.
inference: The comparison does not establish what a confirmed reduction of valine in mutant brain would do. Lower ECHS1 RNA in WWOX cannot establish a matching enzyme defect.
hypothesis: At matched cellular exposure, WWOX may route labeled valine into productive metabolites or disproportionately into the SCPC conjugate.
experiment: Follow labeled valine into protein and mitochondrial products, then test direct pyruvate oxidation and functional recovery with a known ECHS1-deficient control.
limits: Human nutrition data concern ECHS1 and HIBCH deficiencies. Local WWOX exposure and effects on growth, metabolism and spontaneous seizures are unresolved.
